title: CORA Request - Easement (Mayor's Office)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

from the time period of January 1st, 2023 to January 1st, 2024, any email, text, or electronic communications relating to the relinquishment of the subject easement for property Address: "4900-5050 North Race Street" and/or "4900 N Race Street". 

Additional search terms include: Bill file number 23-1478; parcel number - 02144-00-131-000; Project Number: 2023-RELINGQ-0000016-01; site development review - 2022-PROJMSTR-0000280. 

Messages from staff associated with the Denver Mayor's Office, Denver City Council, Denver City Council District 9, Denver Economic and and Opportunity Department and City Planning Department included but not limited to Lucas Palmisano, Jason Gallardo, Brianne White, Victoria Tonikian, Jon Ewing, Michael Johnston, and Darrell Watson.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Sincerely,

Lani Rush

title: Arrest and booking records and booking photos, 2015 to present (Rockville City Police Department)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: Arrest and booking records and booking photos, 2015 to present (Rockville City Police Department)
communications.communication:
Hello,

Thank you so much for the work you do. Under the Maryland Public Information Act, we would be grateful for a copy of the Rockville City Police Department's arrest and booking records, together with booking photographs (image files keyed by booking number) where you keep them, from January 1, 2015, or as far back as your system retains, to the present. Name, date of birth, booking or arrest date, charges and release date would be ideal, as a CSV or spreadsheet sent by reply.

If that is a large lift, the last five years, or any portion that can be shared at no cost, would be wonderful. We kindly ask that fees be waived, and we are happy to narrow the request in any way that helps.

Thank you so much for your time and help.

All the best

title: Unclassified Senior NSC Email Referencing Both the Burgas bus bombing and Damascus Attacks of July 18, 2012 (July 18 – August 18, 2012)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Unclassified Senior NSC Email Referencing Both the Burgas bus bombing and Damascus Attacks of July 18, 2012 (July 18 – August 18, 2012)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) and the Presidential Records Act (44 U.S.C. § 2201 et seq.), I request copies of the following records held by the Barack Obama Presidential Library.

Records requested

Unclassified email messages (sent, received, forwarded, or copied) to or from any of the custodians below, dated July 18, 2012 through August 18, 2012, in which the same message contains:

at least one of: Burgas or Bourgas; and
at least one of: Damascus, Syria, Assad, Assef Shawkat, Shawkat, Shawqat, Rajha, Rajiha, Turkmani, bus bombing.

The subject of the request is the July 18, 2012 attack on a bus of Israeli tourists at Burgas, Bulgaria, and the July 18, 2012 bombing of the National Security Building in Damascus, Syria, including any communication noting, comparing, or discussing a possible relationship between the two events.

Custodians

Priority group (please search and process first):

- Thomas Donilon, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs
- John O. Brennan, Assistant to the President for Homeland Security and Counterterrorism
- Denis McDonough, Deputy National Security Advisor
- Benjamin Rhodes, Deputy National Security Advisor for Strategic Communications

Second group:

- NSC Senior Director for Middle East and North Africa (Steven Simon)
- NSC Senior Director for Iran, Iraq, and the Gulf States (Puneet Talwar)
- NSC Senior Director for Counterterrorism
- NSC Senior Director for European Affairs
- NSC Spokesperson (Tommy Vietor)
- Antony Blinken, Deputy Assistant to the President and National Security Advisor to the Vice President (Office of the Vice President)

Where a named person did not hold the position in July 2012, please search the individual who did.

Collections: The unclassified White House Computer System (WHCS) email accounts of the custodians above.

Scope limits (to keep this request narrow and quick to process)

I am not seeking classified systems, finished intelligence products, or attachments that are intelligence community products. I ask only for the emails and their unclassified attachments.
Please exclude press clippings, news summaries, and mass-distribution messages, and produce only one copy of duplicate messages.

If any responsive record contains classified information, please release the segregable unclassified portions and set the classified material aside for separate mandatory declassification review under E.O. 13526 § 3.5, rather than holding the remainder of the request.

If any record requires consultation or referral to another agency, please release everything else on a rolling basis.

Thank you for the work that the Barack Obama Presidential Library does each day, and thank you for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
